name: oat-project-quick-start
conclusion: oat-project-quick-start (Ask) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 5 autonomy limits, 8 clarification rules, 5 approval gates, 4 validation rules, 3 escalation rules. Strongest: clarification rules.

autonomy_limits.conclusion: 5 autonomy limits (5 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose: implementation code changes; auto-advancing well-understood requests; where dispatch ceilings may be written.

statements.quote: allowed-tools: Read, Write, Bash, Glob, Grep, AskUserQuestion
No implementation code changes.

**Auto-advance rule:** If the request was classified as **well-understood** in Step 2a and discovery surfaced no architecture decisions, component boundary questions, or unexpected complexity, skip th
A project-specific active policy or ceiling must not be written to user `~/.oat/config.json`.
Persist the active project ceiling only in `"$PROJECT_PATH/state.md"`.

clarification_rules.conclusion: 8 clarification rules (8 mandatory, 0 advisory; 4 conditional), mostly list: commit message and project description; inferring requirements from the name; design depth and ladder scope choices.

statements.quote: **Commit now** (recommended when only sync output is dirty) — stage and commit. For sync-only diffs, default the message to `chore: run sync`; otherwise ask the user for the commit message.

If `$ARGUMENTS` contains only a bare `{project-name}` (for example a slug or short title) without a substantive description, ask the user for a short project description before scanning the repo or dr
Do not infer requirements from the project name alone or go exploring the codebase to guess what the project means.
If neither field is available, ask for both the project name and a short project description. One or two sentences is enough for the description.
**One question at a time** — ask focused clarifying questions sequentially, not as a batch. After each answer, update your understanding and let the next question be informed by the response.
Use `AskUserQuestion` to present this choice.
Contradictory or materially incomplete requirements remain a product-judgment boundary; auto-confirmation is not permission to invent scope.
If the effective ladder is missing or incomplete, show the full bundled recommendation and ask the user to select its owning scope before running exactly one command:

approval_gates.conclusion: 5 approval gates (5 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list: dirty working tree choices; buy-in on the chosen direction; requirements confirmation and medium fixes.

statements.quote: Offer three choices via `AskUserQuestion`:
Do not advance past this gate without an explicit choice.
**Incremental validation** — after exploring the solution space and converging on an approach, summarize the chosen direction and get explicit user buy-in before moving to decisions and constraints.
Do not auto-confirm just because the structured question tool is missing.
Apply Critical and Important artifact-local fixes when unambiguous; offer Medium and Minor fixes instead of silently applying them.

validation.conclusion: 4 validation rules (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose: relevant repository checks after formatting; plan artifact review loop; configured gate before completion.

statements.quote: After formatting, run only repository checks relevant to the files changed; writing lifecycle artifacts does not imply unrelated full test suites.
Invoke the shared `Auto Artifact-Review Loop` from `oat-project-plan-writing` with target `plan` before syncing project state or handing off to implementation.
Re-dispatch after rewrites until clean or the retry bound is exhausted.
After artifact finalization and plan artifact review, run the configured gate as the last check before plan and project completion:

escalation.conclusion: 3 escalation rules (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 2 conditional), mostly list: reviewer timeouts; gate attempts exhausted; unresolved dispatch or failed review recording.

statements.quote: After acceptance, poll, nudge, or continue only through the existing reviewer handle. A terminal timeout blocks or escalates without another launch. Replacement eligibility is limited to explicit pre-

`block`: read gate feedback, remediate, and re-run the gate up to `maxAttempts` attempts (default `2`). If attempts are exhausted, escalate to the human with accumulated feedback and append that feedb
If dispatch remains unresolved, review execution fails closed, or the outcome cannot be recorded, leave the Step 3 pre-review values unchanged and commit them before stopping.
